Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and agreed next steps from our call: 

- Scope: FinCo will evaluate Redwood for production inference for customer-facing workflows that handle limited PII (name, email, transaction ids).
- Requirements called out: customer-managed retention windows, per-request access logs (who/what/when), exportable audit logs in CSV/JSON, and EU residency for a subset of workloads (we covered that briefly).

Hi Elena / Marissa —

Attached are two items: (1) audit-log-export-2026-09-30.csv — a redacted CSV export that mirrors the nightly audit export; and (2) access-report-2026-09-30.pdf — a brief summary of access events for the last 24 hours with role annotations.

CSV columns included: timestamp_utc, request_id, model_id, principal_id, principal_type, action, ip_address, region, export_flag, object_size_bytes

Sample row (redacted):
2026-09-30T23:47:12Z, req_4b9f2a, rwd-model-2, user_123, service_account, generate, 18.205.33.10, us-west-2, false, 0

Export delivery: the CSV and PDF are staged in a pre-authenticated, signed S3 URL (7-day expiry). We can also push the file to an SFTP endpoint if FinCo prefers. Let me know the preference and I will generate a fresh link.

Retention: per product policy, audit logs are retained by default for 30 days; for FinCo we can configure a 90-day retention on your dedicated tenant. The retention setting will be applied at provisioning and enforced by the access-control layer; deleted logs are archived for 30 additional days on encrypted storage for recovery (policy change requests will be logged).

Sean — can you add a short security-signed statement for procurement?

- Jordan

Hi Elena —

Short statement from Redwood Security:

Redwood confirms that for dedicated/private tenants we can configure audit log retention to 90 days. Audit logs capture principal identity (user/service account), timestamp, request id, model/resource id, IP address, action taken, and an export flag. Exports are produced as immutable CSV/JSON files and delivered via signed S3 URLs or pushed to customer-managed endpoints. All logs are encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS1.2+). Access to audit logs is restricted via RBAC; only roles with the "audit_reader" permission can request exports.

If you need a signed letter on company letterhead for procurement, we can produce a one-page attestation. Happy to coordinate.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
